context.title: Priests, Levites and Singers
context.summary: The tribe of Levi is traced in detail: the line of high priests from Aaron to the exile, the Levite clans, the temple singers David appointed, and the towns given to the Levites.
context.background: The Levites received no tribal territory; they lived in towns scattered among the tribes. That explains why Samuel's family, linked with Ephraim's hill country in 1 Samuel 1:1, appears here among the Levites (vv. 27–28, 33). Heman, Asaph and Ethan (vv. 33, 39, 44) are names found in psalm titles.

customs.note: Not suburbs in the modern sense, but pasturelands around each town for the Levites' animals.
Towns where someone who killed a person by accident could find protection until a fair hearing.

watchFor: The high-priestly line ends with Jehozadak going into captivity (v. 15).
Aaron's sons alone offer sacrifices; the other Levites assist (vv. 48–49).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

people.name: Merari
people.summary: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Kohath
people.summary: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram (Gen. 46:11).

people.name: Gershon
people.summary: Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Amram
people.summary: The son of Kohath, the son of Levi. He married Jochebed, “his father’s sister,” and was the father of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses (Ex. 6:18, 20; Num. 3:19).

people.name: Uzziel
people.summary: One of the sons of Kohath, and uncle of Aaron (Ex. 6:18; Lev. 10:4).

people.name: Izhar
people.summary: Oil, one of the sons of Kohath, and grandson of Levi (Ex. 6:18, 21; Num. 16:1).

people.name: Hebron
people.summary: The third son of Kohath the Levite (Ex. 6:18; 1 Chr. 6:2, 18).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

people.name: Ithamar
people.summary: Palm isle, the fourth and youngest son of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:3). He was consecrated to the priesthood along with his brothers (Ex. 6:23); and after the death of Nadab and Abihu, he and Eleazar alone discharged the functions of that office (Lev. 10:6, 12; Num. 3:4).

people.name: Abihu
people.summary: Father of Him; i.e., “worshipper of God”, the second of the sons of Aaron (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2; 26:60; 1 Chr. 6:3). Along with his three brothers he was consecrated to the priest’s office (Ex. 28:1).

people.name: Miriam
people.summary: The sister of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 2:4-10; 1 Chr. 6:3). Her name is prominent in the history of the Exodus. She is called “the prophetess” (Ex. 15:20).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah (Ex. 28:1).

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished.

people.name: Abishua
people.summary: The son of Phinehas the high priest (1 Chr. 6:4, 5, 50; Ezra 7:5).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: The son of Bukki, and a descendant of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:5, 51; Ezra 7:4).

people.name: Bukki
people.summary: The son of Abishua.

people.name: Meraioth
people.summary: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:6, 7, 52).

people.name: Ahitub
people.summary: The father of Zadok, who was made high priest by Saul after the extermination of the family of Ahimelech (1 Chr. 6:7, 8; 2 Sam. 8:17).

people.name: Amariah
people.summary: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:7, 52).

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

people.name: Ahimaaz
people.summary: The son and successor of Zadok in the office of high priest (1 Chr. 6:8, 53). On the occasion of the revolt of Absalom he remained faithful to David, and was of service to him in conveying to him tidings of the proceedings of Absalom in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 15:24-37; 17:15-21).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Son of Zadok—the priest.

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: The father of Azariah.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Johanan the father.

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Son of Zadok.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: The Priest.

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Father of Johanan.

people.name: Josedech
people.summary: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile (1 Chr. 6:14, 15). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon.

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: A ruler of the temple (Neh. 11:11).

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Laadan
people.summary: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi (Ex. 6:17; Num. 3:18, 21).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: A son of Gershon.

people.name: Mahli
people.summary: Tribe, in India.

people.name: Mushi
people.summary: Receding, the second of the two sons of Merari (Ex. 6:19; Num. 3:20).

people.name: Zimmah
people.summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:20).

people.name: Adaiah
people.summary: Timely (1 Chr. 6:21).

people.name: Ethan
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:21, 41).

people.name: Korah
people.summary: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution.

people.name: Assir
people.summary: Korah.

people.name: Ebiasaph
people.summary: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: From Rehoboth.

people.name: Tahath
people.summary: Uriel his son.

people.name: Uriel
people.summary: A Kohathite ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr. 6:36).

people.name: Amasai
people.summary: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:25, 35).

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: Prophet of Levi.

people.name: Mahath
people.summary: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah (1 Chr. 6:35).

people.name: Nahath
people.summary: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 6:26).

people.name: Zuph
people.summary: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1); called also Zophai (1 Chr. 6:26).

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: His son.

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: Another Levite of the line of Heman the singer, although he does not seem to have performed any of the usual Levitical offices. He was father of Samuel the prophet (1 Chr. 6:27, 34).

people.name: Elihu
people.summary: The son of Tohu, and grandfather of Elkanah (1 Sam. 1:1).

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1).

people.name: Samuel
people.summary: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son.

people.name: Joel
people.summary: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba (1 Sam. 8:2).

people.name: Abiah
people.summary: The second son of Samuel (1 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chr. 6:28).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: Shimi.

people.name: Uzza
people.summary: Mahli.

people.name: Shimea
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:30).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Heman
people.summary: Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:33; 15:17), to whom the 88th Psalm probably was inscribed.

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Berechiah
people.summary: Son of Shimea, and father of Asaph the musician (1 Chr. 6:39; 15:17).

people.name: Shimea
people.summary: Another Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:39).

people.name: Malchiah
people.summary: Son of Jeaterai.

people.name: Michael
people.summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:40).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:42).

people.name: Jeduthun
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the leaders of the temple music (1 Chr. 6:44; 15:17, 19). He was probably the same as Jeduthun.

people.name: Malluch
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:44).

people.name: Amaziah
people.summary: A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite (1 Chr. 6:45).

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: A Levite.

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: Father of Eliakim.

people.name: Amzi
people.summary: Placed on the left hand side of his brethren to sing in the house of Jehovah, after the ark had rest.

people.name: Shamer
people.summary: Son of Bani.

people.name: Mahli
people.summary: Bon of Mushi and grandson of Merari.

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus.

people.name: Jephunneh
people.summary: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Reuben
people.summary: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4).

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: most holy place
places.summary: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth.

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Eshtemoa
places.summary: Obedience, a town in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 21:14; 1 Chr. 6:57), which was allotted, with the land round it, to the priests. It was frequented by David and his followers during their wanderings; and he sent presents of the spoil of the Amalekites to his friends there (1 Sam. 30:28).

places.name: Jattir
places.summary: Pre-eminent, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:48; 21:14).

places.name: Libnah
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites taken by Joshua (Josh. 10:29-32; 12:15). It became one of the Levitical towns in the tribe of Judah (21:13), and was strongly fortified.

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: A sacerdotal city in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 21:16; 1 Sam. 6:15), on the north border of Judah (Josh. 15:10). It was the scene of an encounter between Jehoash, king of Israel, and Amaziah, king of Judah, in which the latter was made prisoner (2 Kings 14:11, 13).

places.name: Alemeth
places.summary: A sacerdotal city of Benjamin (1 Chr. 6:60), called also Almon (Josh. 21:18), now Almit, a mile north-east of the ancient Anathoth.

places.name: Anathoth
places.summary: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat.

places.name: Geba
places.summary: The hill, (2 Sam. 5:25 [1 Chr. 14:16, “Gibeon”]; 2 Kings 23:8; Neh. 11:31), a Levitical city of Benjamin (1 Kings 15:22; 1 Sam. 13:16; 14:5, wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah (Isa. 10:29; Josh. 18:24, 28).

places.name: Bashan
places.summary: Light soil, first mentioned in Gen. 14:5, where it is said that Chedorlaomer and his confederates “smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth,” where Og the king of Bashan had his residence.

places.name: Gezer
places.summary: A precipice, an ancient royal Canaanitish city (Josh. 10:33; 12:12). It was allotted with its suburbs to the Kohathite Levites (21:21; 1 Chr. 6:67).

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: A city in Samaria (Gen. 33:18), called also Sichem (12:6), Sychem (Acts 7:16). It stood in the narrow sheltered valley between Ebal on the north and Gerizim on the south, these mountains at their base being only some 500 yards apart.

places.name: Beth-horon
places.summary: House of the hollow, or of the cavern, the name of two towns or villages (2 Chr. 8:5; 1 Chr. 7:24) in the territory of Ephraim, on the way from Jerusalem to Joppa.

places.name: Jokmeam
places.summary: Gathering of the people, a city of Ephraim, which was given with its suburbs to the Levites (1 Chr. 6:68).

places.name: Aijalon
places.summary: A city in the tribe of Zebulun (Judg. 12:12), the modern Jalun, three miles north of Cabul.

places.name: Gath-rimmon
places.summary: A Levitical city in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:45; 21:24; 1 Chr. 6:69).

places.name: Aner
places.summary: A city of Manasseh given to the Levites of Kohath’s family (1 Chr. 6:70).

places.name: Ashtaroth
places.summary: A city of Bashan, in the kingdom of Og (Deut. 1:4; Josh. 12:4; 13:12; 9:10). It was in the half-tribe of Manasseh (Josh. 13:12), and as a Levitical city was given to the Gershonites (1 Chr. 6:71).

places.name: Golan
places.summary: Exile, a city of Bashan (Deut. 4:43), one of the three cities of refuge east of Jordan, about 12 miles north-east of the Sea of Galilee (Josh. 20:8).

places.name: Daberath
places.summary: Pasture, a Levitical town of Issachar (Josh. 19:12; 21:28), near the border of Zebulum. It is the modern small village of Deburich, at the base of Mount Tabor.

places.name: Kedesh
places.summary: A city of Issachar (1 Chr. 6:72).

places.name: Anem
places.summary: Two fountains, a Levitical city in the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 6:73).

places.name: Ramoth
places.summary: Heights.

places.name: Abdon
places.summary: One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chr. 8:23).

places.name: Mashal
places.summary: Entreaty, a levitical town in the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 6:74); called Mishal (Josh. 21:30).

places.name: Hukok
places.summary: Decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:34).

places.name: Rehob
places.summary: Another town of Asher (Josh. 19:30), kept possession of by the Canaanites (Judg. 1:31).

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Hammon
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Asher, near Zidon (Josh. 19:28), identified with ‘Ain Hamul.

places.name: Kedesh
places.summary: A “fenced city” of Naphtali, one of the cities of refuge (Josh. 19:37; Judg. 4:6). It was assigned to the Gershonite Levites (Josh. 21:32). It was originally a Canaanite royal city (Josh. 12:22), and was the residence of Barak (Judg. 4:6); and here he and Deborah assembled the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali before the commencement of the conflict with Sisera in the plain of Esdraelon, “for Jehovah among the mighty” (9, 10).

places.name: Kiriathaim
places.summary: A city of refuge in Naphtali (1 Chr. 6:76).

places.name: Tabor
places.summary: A town of Zebulum (1 Chr. 6:77).

places.name: Bezer
places.summary: A city of the Reubenites; one of the three cities of refuge on the east of Jordan (Deut. 4: 43; Josh. 20:8).

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Kedemoth
places.summary: Beginnings; easternmost, a city of Reuben, assigned to the Levites of the family of Merari (Josh. 13:18).

places.name: Mephaath
places.summary: Splendour, a Levitical city (Josh. 21:37) of the tribe of Reuben (13:18).

places.name: Gilead
places.summary: Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” (Gen. 31:25).

places.name: Mahanaim
places.summary: Two camps, a place near the Jabbok, beyond Jordan, where Jacob was met by the “angels of God,” and where he divided his retinue into “two hosts” on his return from Padan-aram (Gen. 32:2).

places.name: Heshbon
places.summary: Intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Josh. 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Num. 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Josh. 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:37).

places.name: Jazer
places.summary: He (God) helps, a city of the Amorites on the east of Jordan, and assigned, with neighbouring places in Gilead, to Gad (Num. 32:1, 35; Josh. 13:25).
